name: Nevada

sales.rateNote: 6.85% is the minimum statewide rate, and every county charges at least that much. It combines the 2.00% state sales tax (NRS 372, State General Fund), the 2.60% Local School Support Tax (NRS 374, State Education Fund), the 0.50% Basic City-County Relief Tax and the 1.75% Supplemental City-County Relief Tax (NRS 377). The part kept for state purposes is 4.60%; the 2.25% relief taxes are levied statewide but go to local governments.

local.levies: Counties can add option taxes on top of the 6.85% minimum, under NRS 377A (public transit, roads, tourism), NRS 377B (infrastructure), NRS 377D, NRS 543 (flood control), NRS 374A (school capital) or special acts and ballot initiatives. Rates are set county-wide, and the minimum rate applies in counties with no option tax.

groceries.note: Unprepared food for home consumption is exempt. Prepared food intended for immediate consumption is taxable; regulation R056-18 sets the rules.

clothing.note: Clothing is tangible personal property and is taxed at the county's full combined rate; the DOT's list of non-taxable items does not include clothing.

sales.holidayNote: No general sales tax holiday. Only active Nevada National Guard members and the relatives who live with them can get a refund of sales tax paid during the Nevada Day observance, October 30 to November 1, 2026, with an exemption letter.

useTax.note: The Consumer Use Tax rate equals the sales tax rate in the buyer's area, including local option taxes (6.85% minimum). It applies to items bought out of state without Nevada sales tax; sales tax paid to another state is credited.

facts.text: The 2.60% Local School Support Tax, part of the 6.85% minimum, goes to the State Education Fund; the 0.50% Basic City-County Relief Tax goes to the county where the sale was made.
Nevada's sales and use tax laws were first enacted in 1955.
Vehicles, aircraft and off-highway vehicles bought in another state for use in Nevada owe Nevada use tax if no sales tax was paid. Proof of tax paid is required to register them.
Separately stated delivery, shipping and postage charges have been non-taxable since May 2009, as are separately listed installation and repair labor.
Nevada National Guard members deployed abroad for at least 30 days can get a letter exempting their purchases from Nevada sales tax for the deployment period.
Nevada became a full member of the Streamlined Sales and Use Tax Governing Board on April 1, 2008.
Sales tax is owed on gross receipts even when a retailer rounds a cash sale to the nearest five cents after the end of penny production in 2025.

property.levied: Local: counties, cities, school districts and special districts set tax rates within a statutory cap, plus a state debt rate. County assessors value property and county treasurers bill and collect.

assessment.text: All taxable property is assessed at 35% of its taxable value (NRS 361.225): a home with a $200,000 taxable value has a $70,000 assessed value. The combined rate is capped at $3.64 per $100 of assessed value, plus 2 cents for state debt outside the cap ($3.66 total). The 2005 abatements (AB 489) also limit the yearly increase in each tax bill.
assessment.capText: Nevada has no flat homestead value exemption on the property tax bill. Instead, the tax on an owner-occupied single-family home that is the owner's primary residence cannot rise more than 3% over the prior year's bill (or less, if the county's general abatement is lower). Any amount above that is abated. The cap does not apply to new construction or to a change of use.

homestead.name: Primary residence partial abatement (3% cap)
homestead.text: Nevada has no flat homestead value exemption on the property tax bill. Instead, the tax on an owner-occupied single-family home that is the owner's primary residence cannot rise more than 3% over the prior year's bill (or less, if the county's general abatement is lower). Any amount above that is abated. The cap does not apply to new construction or to a change of use.

otherRelief.name: General abatement (all other property)
otherRelief.text: Other parcels, including second homes and commercial property, get a cap on tax-bill growth set county by county: the higher of twice the CPI or the county's 9-year average growth in assessed value, but never above 8%.

otherRelief.name: Veterans' Exemption
otherRelief.text: Exempts the first $2,000 of assessed value, indexed to CPI since July 2003, for Nevada-resident veterans with 90 consecutive days of active duty in qualifying periods.

otherRelief.name: Disabled Veterans' Exemption
otherRelief.text: For a permanent service-connected disability: $20,000 of assessed value at 100%, $15,000 at 80-99% and $10,000 at 60-79%, all CPI-indexed since 2003. Surviving spouses also qualify.

otherRelief.name: Blind persons and surviving spouses
otherRelief.text: Property of blind persons is exempt up to $3,000 of assessed value (CPI-adjusted, NRS 361.085); surviving spouses have a partial exemption (NRS 361.080).

dueDates.text: The tax can be paid in four installments: 3rd Monday in August, 1st Monday in October, 1st Monday in January and 1st Monday in March (NRS 361.483). The fiscal year starts July 1 (lien date).

facts.text: Nevada's constitution caps the property tax rate at $5.00 per $100 of assessed value. After the 1979 reform (SB 204, a response to California's Prop 13) the statutory cap became $3.64.
Local government property tax revenue may grow by at most 6% a year (NRS 354.59811): the prior year's revenue x 1.06 is divided by the new assessed value to set the rate.
The state debt rate is 15 cents per $100, inside the cap, plus 2 cents outside the cap added by SB 507 (2003).
Household goods and furniture and business inventories are fully exempt from Nevada property tax.
The Department of Taxation runs a ratio study of each county's assessments every third year and can order a reappraisal if values fall outside the guidelines.
The real property transfer tax base rate is $1.95 for every $500 of value in all counties; some counties add a surcharge.

uncertain: The Nevada Legislature's site (leg.state.nv.us, NRS text) returned 403 (Cloudflare), so no figure was checked against the statute itself; everything comes from Department of Taxation pages and PDFs.

The 6.85% breakdown comes from the DOT 'Components of Sales and Use Tax Rates' PDF (county list dated 07/01/2020, uploaded 12/2024). The DOT sales tax page (2026) confirms 6.85% as the base rate and shows no later change.

The 'Property Tax Elements and Applications' PDF is the 2024 edition (latest online). The $3.64/$3.66 cap, 35% ratio, 15+2 cent state debt rate and abatement rules may have been amended by the 2025 Legislature, which was not checked.
No legal cap on combined county option sales tax rates was found on the DOT site, so cap = null.

The DOT FAQ mentions a 'homestead exemption' among property tax exemptions without describing it; no DOT document describes a homestead value exemption, so the 3% primary-residence abatement is shown as the main relief.
The veterans', disabled veterans' and blind exemption amounts are base figures; the CPI-indexed amounts for fiscal year 2026-27 were not found on the DOT site.
Clothing marked 'taxed' because it is not on the DOT's list of non-taxable items; no explicit DOT statement was found.
